name: ssd-bench-conv-debug-session
notes: Multi-turn conversation: debugging a Rust async runtime issue. system+user+assistant+user chain totalling ~700 tokens. The long assistant turn ensures >= 600 total tokens.

messages.content: You are an expert Rust systems programmer and async runtime specialist. You help engineers debug difficult concurrency issues in production Rust services. You give precise, actionable advice grounded in Rust's ownership model, the tokio runtime, and async/await semantics. When analyzing code, you identify the root cause, explain why it occurs, and provide a corrected version with commentary.

Thank you, that makes sense. I applied Part 1 of your fix. The deadlock is gone, but I am now seeing a different issue: under high concurrency (32 simultaneous requests all with the same prompt hash), I see 32 parallel run_prefill calls all completing, and then 32 duplicate insertions into the cache. The or_insert deduplication works correctly — only one entry survives — but I wasted 31 redundant prefill calls, each taking 1.5 seconds. My GPU cannot handle 32 concurrent forward passes efficiently anyway. How do I implement the per-key flight tracker you mentioned in Part 2? I want: exactly one prefill per distinct prompt hash in-flight at a time, with all other waiters receiving the result of the first call's computation without re-running prefill themselves. The KvBlocks type is Arc<KvBlocks> and is cheaply cloneable.
